svg.title: How the Lab handles a request
svg.desc: A browser on an approved network, such as a jumpbox reached through Azure Bastion, sends a private HTTPS request to the Lab with no Azure keys in the browser (step 1). The Lab is a React web app and FastAPI API in an internal Azure Container Apps environment. It offers chat and agents, Document reviews, Create agent, and Shared history, accepts only the configured catalog, and signs in to Azure services with managed identity. The Lab calls Microsoft Foundry Agent Service through a private endpoint using a configured model deployment (step 2), and the agent result returns to the Lab (step 3). The Lab returns the response to the browser (step 4). Separately, only when a record is saved, the Lab writes Azure Cosmos DB records: chats only when requested, review drafts and results saved by the server, and created-agent metadata; this is not an automatic transcript save (step 5). Azure API Management is optional, outside the default flow, not deployed by default, and not required by the Lab. Caveats: use fictional data only, there is no end-user sign-in, and saved records are shared without per-user authorization.
svg.text: How the Lab handles a request
Numbers 1–4 follow one request; 5 happens only when a record is saved.
What people do in the Lab
Chat with prebuilt or created agents
Prepare and publish Create agent setups
Signs in for Azure service calls
Return agent results to the Lab
Not deployed by default; the Lab does not need it.
Use fictional data only; there is no end-user sign-in.
Saved records are shared, without per-user authorization.
